sentences.text:
THIS CRIMINAL PETITION IS FILED UNDER SECTION 482 OF THE CODE OF CRIMINAL PROCEDURE, 1973 PRAYING TO QUASH THE FIR DATED 30.01.2019 REGISTERED BY PARAPPANA AGRAHARA POLICE, BENGALURU CITY i.e. RESPONDENT AND NOW NUMBERED AS C.C.NO.24797/2019 (CRIME NO.23/2019) REGISTERED UNDER SECTIONS 504, 420, 376, 312, 323, 417 R/W SECTION 34 OF IPC,
WHICH IS PENDING BEFORE THE IX ADDL.C.M.M., BENGALURU CITY AGAINST THE PETITIONER.

THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR FURTHER DICTATION, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

The petitioner/accused No.1 is sought to be prosecuted for the offences punishable under Sections 504, 420, 376, 312, 323, 417 read with Section 34 of IPC.
2.
The case of the prosecution is that, the petitioner along with other accused assaulted and abused the second respondent.

The Chowk Police Station, Kalburagi registered a case in Cr.No.174/2018 and recorded the further statement of the second respondent and also the statement of other witnesses and found that no such incident had taken place.

Hence, the report was sent to the Superintendent of Police Kalburagi, who in turn sent the intimation to the Deputy Commissioner,
Bengaluru.
On transfer of the case, the Deputy Commissioner of Police, Bengaluru sent the report and thereafter a case was registered in Cr.No.23/2019.
The statement of the second respondent was again recorded by the Police Inspector of Parappana Agrahara, and also the statement of other witnesses on 20.07.2019.
The police after completing investigation laid the charge sheet and the petitioner has been arraigned as accused No.1.

The accused Nos.2 to 4 against NC: 2023:KHC:41492 whom similar allegations were made had approached this Court in Crl.P.No.4555/2023 and this Court on 11.02.2021 quashed the proceedings against the accused Nos.2 to 4 by making the following observations:
"5.

Having heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned High Court Government Pleader appearing for the State, on perusal of the records, the Crime Mr. Antariksha Kote vs The State Of Karnataka on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31443647/
2 No.174/2018 was registered at the instance of the complainant-respondent No.2.

sentences.text:
The learned High Court Government Pleader appearing for the State also not disputes the fact that statement of the witnesses was recorded by the Chowk Police and thereafter,
the report in terms of Annexure-'D' dated 03.01.2019 was sent.
6. Having perused the said report, it is clear that no such incident was taken place on 16.08.2018 and statement of witnesses are also negative.
While filing the charge sheet, the Bengaluru Police have recorded the further statement of the complainant and also the statement of one Smt.Mangala.

Having perused the records, the complainant at the first instance has stated nothing with regard to the presence of said Mangala and also in her further statement except stating that the petitioners have abused her in a filthy language, an omnibus statement of allegations have been made against the petitioners that they assaulted her with their hands and that father of the accused No.1 abused over the phone and disconnected the same.
There is nothing on record in support of such allegations.
Inspite of the local police have sent the report that no such incident was taken place, and witnesses have also not spoken anything about the incident, these petitioners have been implicated.
If the proceedings is continued against these petitioners, it amounts to an abuse of process which leads to miscarriage of justice.

Hence, it is appropriate case to invoke Section 482 of Cr.P.C. to quash the proceedings initiated against these petitioners."
3.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties.

The case of the prosecution is that, the petitioner induced the respondent No.2 to have sexual intercourse by promising to marry and after having sexual intercourse, got married in a temple and when the survivor insisted the petitioner to get the marriage registered, the petitioner assaulted and abused her.

The survivor was allegedly in relationship with the petitioner from 5.2.2015 to 31.8.2018 and the marriage of the petitioner with the survivor in a temple was performed in the year 2016 and when the survivor was pregnant, the accused by promising to marry took the survivor on 7.1.2018 to a rented house and committed forcible sexual intercourse till 8.1.2018.
Thereafter, the pregnancy was terminated by the petitioner by making the survivor consume a tablet.

5. Though the incident is alleged to have been taken in the year 2017 and 2018, the FIR was lodged before the police station at Kalburagi on 14.7.2020, which was subsequently transferred to the police at Bengaluru, since the alleged offences of commission of promising to marry and breach of promise to marry was committed within the jurisdiction limits of Bengaluru.

The petitioner and the respondent No.2 were allegedly in relationship from 2014 till 2018 and in the absence of any material that the petitioner at the time of promising to marry induced the survivor to have sexual intercourse with an intention to cheat, the petitioner cannot be prosecuted for the offences alleged against him, NC: 2023:KHC:41492
since the FIR was lodged only after the relationship strained.
Therefore, the continuation of criminal proceedings will be an abuse of the process of law.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
Mr. Antariksha Kote vs The State Of Karnataka on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31443647/
3 ORDER i) Criminal petition is allowed.
ii) The impugned proceeding in CC No.24797/2019 (Crime No.0023/2019) pending on the file of the learned IX Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bangalore City,
insofar as it relates to the petitioner herein, stands quashed.
Sd/-
